**We’re building a new mental‑health journal app.** Since it stores private health‑related data (how people feel each day) and will be used by many people, it’s a **Red**‑level project. That means we’ll set up: - Secure user login (magic‑link or code). - Data isolation: each person can only see and edit their own entries. - Strong privacy notice and data handling. - No payments in version #1, so no billing or webhooks for now. - All secrets (auth, database, AI) live on the server only. Let’s break it into a one‑screen plan. I’ll list the plan first, then ask a couple of quick questions so we can confirm the key details. --- ## One‑screen plan | Section | What I’ll do | |---------|--------------| | **What we’re building** | “A private mental‑health journal where users can write daily notes about how they feel.” | | **Who uses it** | Anyone who wants a safe, personal diary. | | **Risk level** | **Red** – sensitive personal data (health), many users, data isolation required. | | **Day‑one features** | 1. Sign‑up / log‑in (email magic‑link) 2. View diary home (list of past entries) 3. Create / edit a diary entry (rich‑text or simple textarea). | | **Information it stores** | User profile (email, created date). Diary entries: user‑id, timestamp, text. All private – only owner sees them. | | **Logins** | Email‑only magic‑link via Auth service (Supabase Auth – it’s free, built‑in, and secure). | | **Money** | None in v1. 2️⃣ Scaffold Next.js app with fixed routes.
3️⃣ Add auth pages (login, sign‑up).
4️⃣ Create DB table `entries` with RLS rules.
5️⃣ Build diary list & create/edit pages.
6️⃣ Test locally, then deploy to Vercel. | | **Safety** | – Store all API keys in Vercel secrets (not in code).
– RLS rules on DB.
